summary: Redwood AE+SE walked Orbital Health through the Console DeepTrace features — request logs, trace playback, error analysis, and debugging flows. Customer cares about private data handling, ability to replay failing requests, and correlating request traces with their internal logs. Team agreed to run a short replay pilot on staging and exchange security docs.
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Patel: Hi everyone, thanks for joining. we have about an hour, i'm Maya from Redwood, joined by Jonah and Samir on the SE side. Could you quick intros?
[00:07] Priya Rao: Hi Priya Rao, i run ML Ops at Orbital Health. we're investigating inference platforms to stabilize latency and get better debugability on our request failures.
[00:15] Evan Martinez: Evan, SRE, mostly network and infra constraints.
[00:19] Lena Cho: Lena, product - curious about error triage flows.
[00:22] Tom Becker: Tom, security.
[00:24] Jonah Reed: Jonah Reed, SE — i'll do most of the console deep-dive and show trace playback and request forensics.
[00:29] Maya Patel: Great, quick agenda: show console request inspector, tracing, replay, how fallbacks and model variants appear in traces, then map to your network/security Qs and next steps.
[00:40] 
[01:12] Jonah Reed: Alright i'm sharing screen. this is the DeepTrace view, you'll see a request timeline on the left and a list of recent requests on the right. each row has a trace id, model variant, region, and a small latency sparkline. you can filter by status code, token count, and route.
[01:38] Priya Rao: can we filter by a custom request header? we add x-orbital-request-id.
[01:42] Jonah Reed: yes, you can add header-based filters; it's under advanced filters -> header equals. we also auto-ingest trace ids if you forward the header or use the SDK.
[01:52] Evan Martinez: how do we map these traces to our internal logs? we use datadog and have a service trace id.
[01:58] Samir Gupta: two options: 1) send your internal trace id as a header and it will appear in the request metadata, 2) export trace CSV with the header column and join in datadog. we also have a webhook to push matched traces to an endpoint.
[02:12] 
[02:45] Jonah Reed: i'll click a failing request — you can see the full payload preview, token counts, where the failure happened. e.g., this one aborted due to a kv-cache miss and fallback to smaller model, then a 5xx retry. timeline shows model switch at 0.8s then error at 1.1s.
[03:10] Priya Rao: kv-cache miss — do you show the exact cache key? that's sensitive.
[03:16] Jonah Reed: it shows a hashed key by default; we can mask or not collect keys depending on your privacy policy. for Private deployments you control retention and masking via ingestion policies.
[03:27] Tom Becker: KMS? keys at rest? we need to ensure encryption of logs and ability to rotate keys.
[03:33] Maya Patel: yes, Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS/HSM. logs are encrypted at rest and in transit. we can provide our key rotation docs — we'll attach the SOC2 and key handling section.
[03:44] 
[03:59] Jonah Reed: back to the console — the 'playback' button replays the request against a saved model variant in a sandbox environment. this is replay-only and you can set a rate limit on replays to avoid impact. the playback records token-level latency and the exact kernel path used.
[04:23] Lena Cho: does playback re-run in our tenancy or on Redwood's hosted infra?
[04:27] Samir Gupta: for hosted customers playback runs in our sandboxed infra; for Dedicated/Private we can run playback in your VPC/on-prem (pilot decision).
[04:36] Evan Martinez: that matters for PHI — our legal team needs playback to stay in our VPC.
[04:41] Maya Patel: understood — for pilot we can run the replay in a dedicated staging pool in your VPC. we'll include deployment options in the follow-up.
[04:50] 
[05:25] Jonah Reed: showing the error inspector panel — we correlate errors across traces and surface top failing endpoints, a heatmap by prompt length and model variant, and stack traces when available. note: some stack trace text is best-effort from runtime; for strict auditable traces you can forward your own application stacktrace via metadata.
[05:48] Priya Rao: can we set alerts on regression of generation quality?
[05:52] Jonah Reed: yes, Redwood Optimize integrates eval prompt sets and will trigger alerts when BLEU/ROUGE or custom metrics degrade. in the console you can bind a prompt set to a route for continuous regression monitoring.
[06:08] 
[06:40] Evan Martinez: on network: how do you handle model fallbacks across regions? if us-east is overloaded and you route to europe, latency becomes problematic.
[06:48] Samir Gupta: routing policy is configurable per route: prefer region, then fallback region, then model variant. latency thresholds can be set so we avoid cross-region fallbacks unless under X ms.
[06:58] Priya Rao: show me an example trace where fallback happened because of high latency.
[07:03] Jonah Reed: open the example — see here, primary model timed out at 700ms, automatic fallback to quantized variant at 720ms, then cache replay at 760ms. trace shows token-by-token latencies; highest latency was attention kernel on token 34.
[07:25] 
[07:50] Jonah Reed: note on cost visibility — each trace has a token cost estimate and a breakdown of per-segment GPU time. you can use that to identify expensive prompts.
[08:05] Lena Cho: that's helpful for product prioritization — can we send a CSV of top 50 costly prompts?
[08:10] Jonah Reed: yes exportable. we'll include that CSV for your staging replay results.
[08:19] 
[08:45] Jonah Reed: switching to request logs view — shows raw logs, with contextualized segments: request start, model selection, kv cache attempts, kernel selection, and response send. timestamps are approximate to ms.
[09:02] Evan Martinez: what's retention? how long are these logs stored?
[09:06] Maya Patel: retention is configurable; hosted defaults to 30 days, Dedicated can be extended, and Private you control retention. for compliance we can do 90/365 depending on contract.
[09:18] Tom Becker: and audit logs for who viewed what?
[09:20] Samir Gupta: yes RBAC with audit trails. console records read events for traces and exports. we tie that into SSO/SAML and can push to your SIEM.
[09:32] 
[09:58] Jonah Reed: i'll demonstrate a small failure scenario end-to-end: 1) user complaint about hallucination, 2) we locate the request in DeepTrace via header filter, 3) inspect prompt tokens and the kernel path, 4) playback in sandbox, 5) toggle model variant to canonical to reproduce.
[10:20] Priya Rao: do you support deterministic seeds for reproduction?
[10:24] Jonah Reed: yes, for many models we can set a seed or use the recorded RNG state to make deterministic replays; for some non-deterministic layers there are limits but we log RNG metadata.
[10:36] Lena Cho: often our users see occasional long tail times on bigger prompts. can you show percentile latency graphs?
[10:41] Jonah Reed: percentile graphs are on the route dashboard — you get p50/p95/p99 for token latency and total request. here's p95 spike yesterday aligned with a batch-size increase.
[10:54] 
[11:10] Evan Martinez: curious about telemetry export — can we get a kafka sink with trace events?
[11:14] Samir Gupta: yes, exporters include S3/BigQuery/Kafka/webhook. events are JSON-line; you can include or exclude sensitive fields.
[11:24] Tom Becker: for PHI we need data residency — do you support region-limited storage for traces?
[11:29] Maya Patel: yes regional retention and storage, and Private handles on-prem. we'll note that in the security pack.
[11:37] 
[11:58] Jonah Reed: here is a tough one — KV cache thrash. you can see repeated cache misses for the same prefix due to slight prompt variation. console surfaces similar hashes and a suggestion to normalize prefixes or use prefix canonicalization.
[12:19] Priya Rao: hmm we do templating but have slight whitespace diffs between clients. can Redwood do canonicalization heuristics?
[12:25] Jonah Reed: we have a normalization layer you can opt into which canonicalizes whitespace and common punctuation. we can run a transform in ingestion or on the client SDK.
[12:35] 
[12:58] Jonah Reed: switching to the trace correlation tab — you can click a trace and see correlated backend logs (if you forward them), DB queries, and CDN timing in one timeline. this sits behind the trace exporter contract.
[13:15] Evan Martinez: how heavy is the instrumentation? will it add meaningful latency?
[13:19] Samir Gupta: instrumentation is asynchronous; we surface metadata via headers and sidecar logs — typical overhead is single-digit ms for header propagation, none on critical path for token generation.
[13:32] 
[13:58] Priya Rao: security question — who can access playback? we need separation for ops vs eng.
[14:03] Samir Gupta: playback permission is RBAC controlled. you can allow only specific groups to run replays; audit log will show which request id was replayed and by whom.
[14:13] Tom Becker: can playback be disabled entirely?
[14:16] Maya Patel: yes, you can disable playback for the entire account or per-route.
[14:21] 
[14:45] Jonah Reed: small demo: i filtered by header x-orbital-request-id = 7f3c2a and found a set of five attempts. the second attempt shows a model fallback and increase in tokens because we added a system prompt on retry; the trace shows correlation to a downstream lambda timing out at 250ms.
[15:05] Lena Cho: that chain visibility is exactly what product needs — to know if it's our prompt or infra.
[15:09] Jonah Reed: exactly.
[15:12] 
[15:40] Priya Rao: any limitations for on-prem Dedicated? we have g4dn-like hardware and want quantization.
[15:47] Samir Gupta: Dedicated supports quantized runtimes and kernel selection; we ship the inference runtime optimized for common GPUs. for deeply custom kernels we can work with your infra team during onboarding.
[15:59] Evan Martinez: if we run a private deployment, does tracing still go through Redwood control plane?
[16:04] Maya Patel: for Private, the control plane can be customer-managed. you can configure that so traces never leave your network; if you choose Redwood-managed control plane we encrypt in transit and hold metadata per contract.
[16:18] 
[16:45] Jonah Reed: wrapping up with a sample pilot plan: 1) 1-week staging replay to reproduce 5 failure patterns; 2) collect p95/p99 latency and cost breakdown; 3) prove playback in your VPC for compliance; 4) recommend KV canonicalization and route-level fallback policy.
[17:05] Priya Rao: timeline — we prefer a pilot next week and will provide dataset and IDs by monday.
[17:12] Maya Patel: we'll aim to start replay on 2026-04-06 pending your sample data. i'll send SOC2 and network diagrams today.
[17:20] 
[17:45] Tom Becker: last question: exportable tamper-evident audit trail?
[17:49] Samir Gupta: yes we support signed audit exports and can integrate with your SIEM; includes who/when/action and hash chaining for tamper evidence.
[17:58] Lena Cho: great, thanks.
[18:02] Maya Patel: recap of next steps and action items, we'll follow up with a calendar invite for pilot kickoff. thanks everyone.

Notes on transcript: occasional mis-recognitions (e.g., "kv cache" heard as "K V cache"), filler words and interruptions preserved. Some technical terms abbreviated in speech.
notes: Customer strongly prefers playback inside their VPC for PHI compliance.
Pilot will focus on replaying 5 error scenarios and producing p95/p99 latency + cost CSVs.
Security follow-up (SOC2, KMS, audit exports) is high priority for Tom.
